title: Variational lower bound
question: What is the lower bound on the log marginal likelihood used in variational inference?
notes: Gold corrected on 2026-09-12 after reading the source. The bound L(q,theta) is derived in section 9.4 (PDF pages 469-470) and reused for variational inference in 10.1; the original gold named 10.1 only, which scored a correct retrieval into 9.4 as a miss. Shares heavy vocabulary with 10.2 through 10.7, so a landing in a neighbouring variational section is still a miss.

title: Responsibilities defined then used

title: Design matrix and normal equations

notes: Definition and use are close together here, which makes this the control for W03-15: if the contextual arm helps on 15 but not 16, the help is coming from context restoration rather than from the prefix acting as extra keywords.

title: Kernel functions

notes: Both gold sections are tiny (2 and 4 pages) and both titles are parser-damaged. Tests whether small gold spans are findable at all.

title: EM monotonicity conditions
question: Under what conditions does the EM algorithm guarantee that the likelihood does not decrease?
notes: The guarantee is conditional. Retrieving the claim without its conditions is the scope-inversion failure the week note flagged as the dangerous one, because nothing in the output looks wrong.

title: When Laplace approximation fails
question: When does the Laplace approximation give a poor approximation to the posterior?
notes: Four-page gold section. The limitations are stated as qualifications on an otherwise positive presentation, so a chunk that keeps only the method description inverts the answer.

title: Conditional independence assumptions
question: What conditional independence assumptions does the naive Bayes model make and when are they violated?
notes: 'When are they violated' is the half most likely to be chunked away from the half that states the assumption.

title: PCA versus probabilistic PCA
question: How does probabilistic PCA differ from conventional principal component analysis?
notes: A comparison cannot be answered from one side of it. Coverage of both sections matters more than raw recall.

title: Two routes to complexity control

notes: The two sections are not adjacent and share little vocabulary with each other. Hardest multi-hop case in the set.
